headline: This 2022 law directs USAID to run programs that prevent and treat malnutrition in other countries, with reporting to Congress and a seven-year sunset.
what_it_does: The law tells the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) to carry out activities that prevent and treat malnutrition around the world. USAID may coordinate with other federal agencies through a Global Nutrition Coordination Plan and may establish a Nutrition Leadership Council. The agency must pick target countries using specified malnutrition indicators, update that list within five years, and direct resources to the people most at risk of severe malnutrition. USAID must also give Congress an implementation plan and annual reports, and the act's provisions end seven years after enactment.

who_it_affects.group: People in countries with high rates of malnutrition, especially those at risk of severe malnutrition
who_it_affects.how: USAID is directed to target prevention and treatment programs toward the countries and populations most affected.

who_it_affects.group: USAID and other federal agencies working on global nutrition
who_it_affects.how: The agency must set up a country-selection process, produce an implementation plan and annual reports, and may coordinate through an interagency council and plan.
USAID may work with the agency's board of directors on nutrition efforts under this law.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 19, 2022; the provisions terminate seven years after enactment.
